clocks.cve: The CVE clock is NVD's publication date (`published`). It is not the first day NVD's record held both an impact statement and a configuration for the product (detectable_at), which this output does not compute.
clocks.kev_date_added: CISA KEV dateAdded as NVD mirrors it in `cisaExploitAdd`. The mirror lags CISA; it is not the date of first exploitation.
clocks.promotion_date: The day the vendor's release blog announces a major's promotion to stable, read by hand from the post each row of the promotion table cites. It moves when the `skip` device may install a release; it is never shown as a release date, and the timeline's date still says which build predates a fix.
clocks.published: NVD `published`, truncated to the UTC date.
clocks.release_date: The date Mozilla's product-details gives the version's own release-channel row (its `date`, a calendar day with no time or zone). An ESR row of the same version keeps its own date and is not read here. Source: Mozilla's product-details for Firefox (firefox.json), release channel, https://product-details.mozilla.org/1.0/firefox.json, fetched 2026-11-24T22:24:44Z.
clocks.severity: Today's score: CVSS v3.1, else v4.0, else v2, NVD's Primary entry first. No score history is held.

definitions.branch: A release line is the first BRANCH_COMPONENTS components of a version. A range is branch-ambiguous when it matches catalog releases on a line other than its fixed version's: the fix for that other line cannot be read from the range.
definitions.candidates: CVEs whose NVD configurations name the product's CPE pair, plus CVEs with no configurations whose CNA affected block names the product. RULED 2026-10-02: the second kind is excluded and counted, never placed from the CNA block; another source of ranges is a later benchmark, added beside this one.
definitions.critical_or_kev: TABLED 2026-10-02, not ruled: do not quote this row. As computed, a release is installed on the first day a CVE it fixes is KEV-listed or critical, and never before the timeline's release date. No score history is held, so today's NVD score stands in for the score on that day and a critical CVE triggers on its publication date.
definitions.cve_clock: A CVE is placed by NVD's publication date: it is in the window when NVD published it inside the window, and its exposure is counted from that day.
definitions.device: RULED 2026-10-02. The device is one bundle id, and only releases filed under it are replayed. For a release table it is the bundle id the table names.
definitions.early_stable: RULED 2026-10-03. Promotion dates come from the vendor's release blog, held as a hand-captured table (`sharedAssets/rules/promotions.json`): one row per major, with the post it was read from. A release the timeline dates before its major's promotion day is early stable. `skip` installs it no earlier than that day and never installs a major above the table's newest row. `take` installs every listed release on its release date. The policy numbers are `skip` for a product the table holds rows for and `take` for every other; the table is kept by hand, one row per major. Where the table holds no row (another product, or a major older than its oldest row) the catalog rule stands in and is not to be quoted: for a product with one release line, early is the first day the timeline dates a major, or an older major still dated more than a day later, or a major above the timeline's current version, and `skip` never installs such a release. On a table that names an edition the catalog rule is not applied (see `edition`).
definitions.edition: RULED 2026-11-24 (Mozilla's channels and NVD's editions, adopted with the day-walk plan). Applies only when the release table names an edition (`timeline.edition`); otherwise every statement NVD makes about the product's CPE pairs is applied. For the release edition, a statement whose sw_edition is `esr`, or whose product is the pair's `_esr` twin (`firefox_esr`), is about the other edition and is not applied; `-` and unmarked `*` statements are. A CVE left with no statement is excluded as `other_edition_only`. So is one whose applied statements are all unmarked ranges that end on an ESR line (a minor of 1 or more on a major in `timeline.esr_majors`, as `< 128.5.0` does) when none of them holds the release the timeline dates as newest on the day before NVD published the CVE (`edition_signal: bound_shape`). When one holds it, a release-channel device was running an affected build as NVD published the CVE, and the ranges are applied as stated (`edition_signal: current_release_in_range`): NVD writes a fix shipped in Firefox 154 and ESR 153.1 on one day as `141.0 ..< 153.1.0`, a range that ends on an ESR line and holds every release build up to 153.0.x. That test was added on review on 2026-11-24 and adopted 2026-11-25 (ruling 16). A statement whose sw_edition and end disagree (`esr` ending on a release line, `-` ending on an ESR line) is taken at its sw_edition, and its CVE is counted in `counts.edition_conflicts` with `edition_signal: conflict`. On a table that names an edition no release is early stable: every row is a build the vendor shipped on that channel, so the catalog rule is not applied (`early_stable_read_from: release_channel`) and the `skip` and `take` devices are one device.
definitions.exposure_days: Days on or after publication on which the installed version is inside an affected range: the fixing release's install date minus the publication date, cut off at the window's last day when no fix was installed (`open_at_window_end`).
definitions.fixed_version: An excluded range end is the fixed version. After an inclusive end or an exact version it is the next catalog release on the same line that no range of the CVE matches.
definitions.fixed_version_not_a_catalog_release: RULED 2026-10-02. When the excluded range end is not a catalog release (another platform's build, or a typo at NVD), the fix is the first catalog release on the bound's line at or above it, under its own method `first_catalog_release_at_or_above_end_excluded` and never `range_end_excluded`. `fixed_version_not_in_catalog` is kept for the case where the catalog holds no release at or above the bound.
definitions.install: RULED 2026-10-02. A policy of D days installs each release by the D-th day, and the day the timeline dates the release is day one: the install date is the release date + (D - 1) days. One update event per day on which the installed version rises.
definitions.never: The device stays on the version that was current when the window opened.
definitions.never_seen: The device ran no affected version on or after the CVE's NVD publication date: the fixing release was installed on or before that date, or the versions it ran were never inside an affected range (`never_seen_outside_affected_range`).
definitions.path: RULED 2026-10-02: the policy numbers are `hold` — the device stays at or below the release line current when the window opened. `latest` follows the newest release across lines and is the alternative.
definitions.platform: RULED 2026-10-02. Whether a CVE is about the observer's platform is read from NVD's configuration and from nothing else, in both directions: the description is not consulted.
definitions.prerelease: A criterion `parse.py` reads as naming a pre-release (`4.4.9:rc0`) is not applied to a release build; it is counted in `criteria_skipped`.
definitions.release_reported_before_its_fix: RULED 2026-10-02. A release at or above the fixed version that the timeline dates before the fixed version does not clear the CVE: the device stays exposed until it runs a release dated on or after the fix. Chrome's early stable builds of the next major are the case: 155 is above every 154 fix by number, and nothing held says an earlier build carries a later fix. Also ruled: a build of the fixed version's own train (the same but for the last component, `130.0.6723.70` beside `.69`) carries the fix whatever order the timeline dates them in.
definitions.steady_state: A D-day device opens the window on the newest release whose install date had already passed. `never` and `critical_or_kev` open it on the newest release the timeline had dated by the window's first day.
definitions.timeline: Releases and their dates are one public release table, named in `timeline`: `name`, `url`, `fetched_at` and `sha256` say which source and which copy of it, `clock` what its date means, and `rule` which of the source's rows were dropped. A catalog release, anywhere in these definitions, is a release this table lists, and the timeline's current version is the newest it dates on or before the earlier of the window's requested last day and the day before the table was fetched: the window's last day before any promotion-table cut, which that version decides.
definitions.window: The window opens two years before its requested last day unless `since` is given. The requested last day is `until`, or the day before the table was fetched. It is cut short at either end, never moved: never past the day before the table was fetched, because a table knows nothing of a release after it was read; for a product the promotion table holds rows for, never on or past the first day the timeline dates a major the promotion table has no row for, because from then on the waiting device's numbers would rest on a promotion day nobody has read (clamp ruled 2026-11-24); and never before the first day a 60-day device runs a release the table lists (59 days after the table's first release, or after the first day the device that waits for promotion may install one, if that is later), because the version a device ran before the table's first release is not in the table. Where the table says its channel began inside the window (`timeline.channel_start`), the window opens 59 days after that day, the first day a 60-day device has one of the channel's releases installed. Each cut is in `window.shortened_by`.
